title_suggestion: The Hidden Scale of the Hawaiian Chain

format.medium: 3D satellite map and geological cross-section diagram

style: Stylised 2.5D topographic satellite relief map across deep ocean waters, transitioning into a flat cross-section geological diagram. Warm glowing neon outlines highlight landmasses and magma plumes against cool navy oceanic backgrounds. Clean, smooth orbital camera pans and zooms.
narration: Curious, educational, and steady at a brisk informative pace.
never_change: The deep blue ocean backdrop, warm golden island highlighting, and clean sans-serif callout labels.

facts.detail: Hawaii is commonly depicted as just eight primary islands.
Four of the primary Hawaiian islands are significantly larger.
Four companion islands make up the smaller half of the main group.
Placing the eight main islands beside the continental United States makes them appear tiny.
The full island chain actually encompasses 137 individual volcanic islands and atolls trailing northwest.
The entire archipelago extends across roughly 1,500 miles.
Superimposed on the continental mainland, the full span covers the distance from California across to Texas.
The visible islands represent merely the highest summits of a massive underwater volcanic ridge.
A stationary mantle plume generates magma beneath the moving Pacific oceanic plate.
Because the crust moves over an anchored thermal plume, volcanic ridges form consecutively over millions of years.
Northwest plate movement places the youngest islands at the southeastern end.
Midway Atoll represents one of the ancient remnant atolls along the chain.
Midway served as a key historical military post and the site of a pivotal World War II naval clash.
Geographically part of the chain, Midway is politically an unorganized federal territory rather than state land.
Its runway remains designated as an emergency landing strip for transoceanic flights.
